recipes.title: Moroccan zaalouk with cucumber, light
recipes.summary: Roasted eggplant and tomato are cooked down with garlic, cumin and paprika, then served with crisp cucumber. The lighter version uses less oil and extra vegetables.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C so the eggplant roasts rather than steams.
Cut the eggplant into large cubes and spread it across a wide baking tray.
Toss the eggplant with half the olive oil, cumin and paprika until every piece is lightly coated.
Roast the eggplant until collapsed, browned at the edges and tender all the way through.
Cook the garlic in the remaining olive oil until fragrant but not browned.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and simmer until they become thick and spoonable.
Fold the roasted eggplant into the tomatoes and mash a few pieces to give the zaalouk a rustic texture.
Stir the lemon juice and cilantro through the warm zaalouk.
Cut the cucumber into thick batons for scooping the zaalouk.
Rest the zaalouk until warm or room temperature before serving it with the cucumber.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served warm or at room temperature. Refrigerate the zaalouk for up to 4 days and keep the cucumber separate so it stays crisp. Freeze only the zaalouk for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Spanish tortilla, light
recipes.summary: A protein-rich Spanish tortilla with plenty of softly cooked onion, tender potato and eggs. Less oil and potato keep the lighter version balanced without changing its character.

steps.instruction: Slice the potato and onion thinly so they soften evenly without browning too quickly.
Heat most of the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat.
Cook the potato and onion gently until completely tender but still pale, turning them carefully from time to time.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl until the whites and yolks are evenly combined.
Drain any loose olive oil from the potato and onion, then fold them into the eggs.
Rest the egg mixture so the potato absorbs some of the egg and the tortilla holds together.
Coat the pan with the remaining olive oil and pour in the egg mixture.
Cook the tortilla over medium-low heat until the base is golden and the top is mostly set.
Invert the tortilla onto a plate and slide it back into the pan.
Cook the second side until golden while the centre remains tender and moist.
Rest the Spanish tortilla before slicing so it sets cleanly.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve warm or at room temperature. Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently in a covered pan, or enjoy cold. Freezing is not recommended because the potato becomes grainy.

recipes.title: Middle Eastern beef kofta with tahini, light
recipes.summary: Grilled beef kofta with roasted eggplant, crisp cucumber and lemony tahini. The lighter plate keeps the protein generous while leaning on extra vegetables and less sauce.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C and heat a grill pan over medium-high heat.
Cut the eggplant into thick wedges and arrange it on a baking tray.
Coat the eggplant with half the olive oil and a little of the cumin and paprika.
Roast the eggplant until browned at the edges and soft in the centre.
Mix the ground beef with the onion, garlic, remaining cumin, remaining paprika and half the cilantro.
Shape the ground beef mixture into short oval kofta around flat skewers or into compact logs.
Brush the kofta with the remaining olive oil.
Grill the kofta until browned outside and cooked through at the centre.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice until smooth and spoonable.
Slice the cucumber and toss it with the remaining cilantro.
Rest the kofta briefly so the juices settle.
Serve the kofta with the roasted eggplant, cucumber and tahini sauce.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the cooked kofta and roasted eggplant for up to 3 days. Keep the cucumber and tahini sauce separate. Freeze the kofta for up to 2 months, but serve the vegetables fresh.

recipes.title: Mexican garlic shrimp tacos, light
recipes.summary: Juicy garlic shrimp with smoky cumin and paprika, tucked into warm tortillas with crisp lime-dressed cabbage. Fewer tortillas and extra cabbage keep this pescatarian dinner light.

steps.instruction: Shred the green cabbage, slice the onion and chop the garlic and cilantro.
Toss the shrimp with the cumin, paprika and half the olive oil.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a wide frying pan over high heat.
Cook the onion until softened at the edges and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink, curled and opaque throughout.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan until soft and flexible.
Toss the green cabbage with half the lime and the cilantro.
Fill the tortilla with the shrimp, onion and dressed green cabbage, then serve with the remaining lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled fresh. Refrigerate the cooked shrimp and onion for up to 2 days. Keep the tortilla and dressed green cabbage separate, and do not freeze the assembled tacos.

recipes.title: Brazilian cinnamon fried bananas, light
recipes.summary: Ripe banana cooked until golden and finished with a light dusting of cinnamon. This simple Brazilian-style snack is warm, soft and gently caramelised.

ingredients.name: banana
ingredients.preparation: ripe but firm, peeled and halved lengthwise

steps.instruction: Peel the banana and halve each one lengthwise without breaking the pieces.
Measure the cinnamon into a small bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium heat.
Fry the banana until golden and caramelised underneath.
Turn the banana carefully and cook until the second side is golden and soft at the centre.
Sprinkle the cinnamon over the hot banana.
Rest the fried banana briefly before serving so the surface caramel sets slightly.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served warm. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat briefly in a dry pan. Freezing is not recommended because the banana becomes watery after thawing.
